beats.speech: Stop saying very. You're going to practise sixty better words to use instead. Listen to each word and its example sentence, then repeat the sentence out loud in the pause. You don't need to look at the screen. Let's start.
Part 1. Stop saying very big.

card.headline: Huge
card.example: We grew a huge pumpkin this year.

beats.speech: Huge. It means extremely big. We grew a huge pumpkin this year.

card.headline: Giant
card.example: The farmer won a prize for his giant pumpkin.

beats.speech: Giant. It means much bigger than normal. The farmer won a prize for his giant pumpkin.

card.headline: Enormous
card.example: An enormous mountain rose above the village.

beats.speech: Enormous. It means extremely large. An enormous mountain rose above the village.

card.headline: Massive
card.example: A massive rock blocked the road.

beats.speech: Massive. It means very large and heavy. A massive rock blocked the road.

card.headline: Vast
card.example: Sheep grazed in vast green fields.

beats.speech: Vast. It means extremely large in area. Sheep grazed in vast green fields.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
We grew a huge pumpkin this year.
The farmer won a prize for his giant pumpkin.
An enormous mountain rose above the village.
A massive rock blocked the road.
Sheep grazed in vast green fields.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | We grew a huge pumpkin this year. | The farmer won a prize for his giant pumpkin. | An enormous mountain rose above the village. | A massive rock blocked the road. | Sheep grazed in vast green fields.
Part 2. Stop saying very good.

card.headline: Excellent
card.example: That's an excellent idea.

beats.speech: Excellent. It means extremely good. That's an excellent idea.

card.headline: Superb
card.example: We had a superb meal by the sea.

beats.speech: Superb. It means of the highest quality. We had a superb meal by the sea.

card.headline: Fantastic
card.example: Our hotel room had a fantastic view.

beats.speech: Fantastic. It means wonderful, amazing. Our hotel room had a fantastic view.

card.headline: Outstanding
card.example: She got an outstanding result in her exam.

beats.speech: Outstanding. It means much better than the rest. She got an outstanding result in her exam.

card.headline: Brilliant
card.example: That's a brilliant plan!

beats.speech: Brilliant. It means very clever, or extremely good. That's a brilliant plan!

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
That's an excellent idea.
We had a superb meal by the sea.
Our hotel room had a fantastic view.
She got an outstanding result in her exam.
That's a brilliant plan!

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | That's an excellent idea. | We had a superb meal by the sea. | Our hotel room had a fantastic view. | She got an outstanding result in her exam. | That's a brilliant plan!
Part 3. Stop saying very happy.

card.headline: Thrilled
card.example: I'm thrilled with the result.

beats.speech: Thrilled. It means very excited and pleased. I'm thrilled with the result.

card.headline: Delighted
card.example: I'm delighted to see you.

beats.speech: Delighted. It means very pleased. I'm delighted to see you.

card.headline: Overjoyed
card.example: They were overjoyed at the news.

beats.speech: Overjoyed. It means extremely happy about something. They were overjoyed at the news.

card.headline: Ecstatic
card.example: Ecstatic fans filled the streets.

beats.speech: Ecstatic. It means extremely happy and excited. Ecstatic fans filled the streets.

card.headline: Elated
card.meaning: very happy and excited, often after a success
card.example: The team was elated after the win.

beats.speech: Elated. It means very happy and excited, often after a success. The team was elated after the win.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
I'm thrilled with the result.
I'm delighted to see you.
They were overjoyed at the news.
Ecstatic fans filled the streets.
The team was elated after the win.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | I'm thrilled with the result. | I'm delighted to see you. | They were overjoyed at the news. | Ecstatic fans filled the streets. | The team was elated after the win.
Part 4. Stop saying very tired.

card.headline: Exhausted
card.meaning: so tired you have no energy left
card.example: I was exhausted after the marathon.

beats.speech: Exhausted. It means so tired you have no energy left. I was exhausted after the marathon.

card.headline: Drained
card.example: I felt drained after a long meeting.

beats.speech: Drained. It means tired in body and mind. I felt drained after a long meeting.

card.headline: Worn out
card.example: We were worn out after moving house.

beats.speech: Worn out. It means tired from hard work. We were worn out after moving house.

card.headline: Shattered
card.example: She was shattered after a night shift.

beats.speech: Shattered. It means extremely tired. She was shattered after a night shift. This one is British and informal.

card.headline: Weary
card.meaning: tired after doing something for a long time
card.example: They were weary after a long journey.

beats.speech: Weary. It means tired after doing something for a long time. They were weary after a long journey.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
I was exhausted after the marathon.
I felt drained after a long meeting.
We were worn out after moving house.
She was shattered after a night shift.
They were weary after a long journey.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | I was exhausted after the marathon. | I felt drained after a long meeting. | We were worn out after moving house. | She was shattered after a night shift. | They were weary after a long journey.
Part 5. Stop saying very bad.

card.headline: Terrible
card.example: A terrible storm hit the coast.

beats.speech: Terrible. It means very bad or serious. A terrible storm hit the coast.

card.headline: Awful
card.example: There's an awful smell in the kitchen.

beats.speech: Awful. It means extremely bad or unpleasant. There's an awful smell in the kitchen.

card.headline: Dreadful
card.example: I made a dreadful mistake.

beats.speech: Dreadful. It means very bad. You'll hear it a lot in British English. I made a dreadful mistake.

card.headline: Horrible
card.example: I've had a horrible day.

beats.speech: Horrible. It means very unpleasant, or unkind. I've had a horrible day.

card.headline: Atrocious
card.example: The weather was atrocious all week.

beats.speech: Atrocious. It means shockingly bad. The weather was atrocious all week.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
A terrible storm hit the coast.
There's an awful smell in the kitchen.
I made a dreadful mistake.
I've had a horrible day.
The weather was atrocious all week.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | A terrible storm hit the coast. | There's an awful smell in the kitchen. | I made a dreadful mistake. | I've had a horrible day. | The weather was atrocious all week.
Part 6. Stop saying very small.

card.headline: Tiny
card.example: Their kitchen is tiny.

beats.speech: Tiny. It means extremely small. Their kitchen is tiny.

card.headline: Minuscule
card.meaning: so small it is hard to notice
card.example: There was only a minuscule amount of sugar left.

beats.speech: Minuscule. It means so small it is hard to notice. There was only a minuscule amount of sugar left.

card.headline: Microscopic
card.meaning: too small to see without a microscope
card.example: Pond water is full of microscopic creatures.

beats.speech: Microscopic. It means too small to see without a microscope. Pond water is full of microscopic creatures.

card.headline: Miniature
card.meaning: much smaller than the real thing
card.example: He collects miniature trains.

beats.speech: Miniature. It means much smaller than the real thing. He collects miniature trains.

card.headline: Compact
card.meaning: small and designed to save space
card.example: We rented a compact car for the city.

beats.speech: Compact. It means small and designed to save space. We rented a compact car for the city.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Their kitchen is tiny.
There was only a minuscule amount of sugar left.
Pond water is full of microscopic creatures.
He collects miniature trains.
We rented a compact car for the city.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Their kitchen is tiny. | There was only a minuscule amount of sugar left. | Pond water is full of microscopic creatures. | He collects miniature trains. | We rented a compact car for the city.

Part 7. Stop saying very sad.

card.headline: Miserable
card.example: He felt miserable after losing his job.

beats.speech: Miserable. It means very unhappy or uncomfortable. He felt miserable after losing his job.

card.headline: Heartbroken
card.meaning: extremely sad because of love or loss
card.example: She was heartbroken when her dog died.

beats.speech: Heartbroken. It means extremely sad because of love or loss. She was heartbroken when her dog died.

card.headline: Devastated
card.example: They were devastated by the news.

beats.speech: Devastated. It means very shocked and sad. They were devastated by the news.

card.headline: Gloomy
card.example: He felt gloomy on a rainy Monday morning.

beats.speech: Gloomy. It means sad and without hope. He felt gloomy on a rainy Monday morning.

card.headline: Down in the dumps
card.example: I've been down in the dumps all week.

beats.speech: Down in the dumps. It means sad and without energy. I've been down in the dumps all week. This one is informal.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
He felt miserable after losing his job.
She was heartbroken when her dog died.
They were devastated by the news.
He felt gloomy on a rainy Monday morning.
I've been down in the dumps all week.

Part 8. Stop saying very angry.

card.headline: Furious
card.example: She was furious about the broken window.

beats.speech: Furious. It means extremely angry. She was furious about the broken window.

card.headline: Livid
card.example: My dad was livid when he saw the bill.

beats.speech: Livid. It means absolutely furious. My dad was livid when he saw the bill.

card.headline: Outraged
card.meaning: angry and shocked because something is unfair
card.example: People were outraged by the decision.

beats.speech: Outraged. It means angry and shocked because something is unfair. People were outraged by the decision.

card.headline: Fuming
card.meaning: very angry, often without saying anything
card.example: He sat in the traffic jam, fuming.

beats.speech: Fuming. It means very angry, often without saying anything. He sat in the traffic jam, fuming.

card.headline: Irate
card.meaning: very angry, often because you were treated badly
card.example: An irate customer demanded to speak to the manager.

beats.speech: Irate. It means very angry, often because you were treated badly. An irate customer demanded to speak to the manager.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
She was furious about the broken window.
My dad was livid when he saw the bill.
People were outraged by the decision.
He sat in the traffic jam, fuming.
An irate customer demanded to speak to the manager.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | She was furious about the broken window. | My dad was livid when he saw the bill. | People were outraged by the decision. | He sat in the traffic jam, fuming. | An irate customer demanded to speak to the manager.
Part 9. Stop saying very beautiful.

card.headline: Gorgeous
card.example: You look gorgeous in that dress.

beats.speech: Gorgeous. It means very beautiful and attractive. You look gorgeous in that dress.

card.headline: Stunning
card.meaning: so beautiful that it surprises you
card.example: The view from the top was stunning.

beats.speech: Stunning. It means so beautiful that it surprises you. The view from the top was stunning.

card.headline: Breathtaking
card.example: The sunset over the sea was breathtaking.

beats.speech: Breathtaking. It means extremely beautiful and impressive. The sunset over the sea was breathtaking.

card.headline: Exquisite
card.meaning: beautiful, delicate and made with great skill
card.example: She wore an exquisite silver necklace.

beats.speech: Exquisite. It means beautiful, delicate and made with great skill. She wore an exquisite silver necklace.

card.headline: Radiant
card.example: The bride looked radiant.

beats.speech: Radiant. It means beautiful and shining with happiness. The bride looked radiant.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
You look gorgeous in that dress.
The view from the top was stunning.
The sunset over the sea was breathtaking.
She wore an exquisite silver necklace.
The bride looked radiant.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | You look gorgeous in that dress. | The view from the top was stunning. | The sunset over the sea was breathtaking. | She wore an exquisite silver necklace. | The bride looked radiant.
Part 10. Stop saying very scared.

card.headline: Terrified
card.example: I'm terrified of spiders.

beats.speech: Terrified. It means extremely scared. I'm terrified of spiders.

card.headline: Petrified
card.meaning: so scared that you cannot move
card.example: He was petrified when the lights went out.

beats.speech: Petrified. It means so scared that you cannot move. He was petrified when the lights went out.

card.headline: Horrified
card.example: We were horrified by the accident.

beats.speech: Horrified. It means scared and shocked. We were horrified by the accident.

card.headline: Panic-stricken
card.meaning: so scared that you cannot think clearly
card.example: The panic-stricken crowd ran for the exit.

beats.speech: Panic-stricken. It means so scared that you cannot think clearly. The panic-stricken crowd ran for the exit.

card.headline: Scared stiff
card.example: I was scared stiff during the horror film.

beats.speech: Scared stiff. It means extremely scared. I was scared stiff during the horror film. This one is informal.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
I'm terrified of spiders.
He was petrified when the lights went out.
We were horrified by the accident.
The panic-stricken crowd ran for the exit.
I was scared stiff during the horror film.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | I'm terrified of spiders. | He was petrified when the lights went out. | We were horrified by the accident. | The panic-stricken crowd ran for the exit. | I was scared stiff during the horror film.
Part 11. Stop saying very important.

card.headline: Crucial
card.meaning: extremely important, because other things depend on it
card.example: Sleep is crucial for your health.

beats.speech: Crucial. It means extremely important, because other things depend on it. Sleep is crucial for your health.

card.headline: Essential
card.example: Water is essential for life.

beats.speech: Essential. It means completely necessary. Water is essential for life.

card.headline: Vital
card.meaning: necessary to succeed or to stay alive
card.example: It is vital to wear a seat belt.

beats.speech: Vital. It means necessary to succeed or to stay alive. It is vital to wear a seat belt.

card.headline: Critical
card.meaning: extremely important at a particular moment
card.example: The next few minutes are critical.

beats.speech: Critical. It means extremely important at a particular moment. The next few minutes are critical.

card.headline: Paramount
card.example: Safety is paramount on a building site.

beats.speech: Paramount. It means more important than anything else. Safety is paramount on a building site. This one is formal.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Sleep is crucial for your health.
Water is essential for life.
It is vital to wear a seat belt.
The next few minutes are critical.
Safety is paramount on a building site.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Sleep is crucial for your health. | Water is essential for life. | It is vital to wear a seat belt. | The next few minutes are critical. | Safety is paramount on a building site.
Part 12. Stop saying very interesting.

card.headline: Fascinating
card.example: The documentary about whales was fascinating.

beats.speech: Fascinating. It means extremely interesting. The documentary about whales was fascinating.

card.headline: Captivating
card.meaning: so interesting that it holds all your attention
card.example: She gave a captivating speech.

beats.speech: Captivating. It means so interesting that it holds all your attention. She gave a captivating speech.

card.headline: Gripping
card.meaning: so exciting that you cannot stop reading or watching
card.example: It was a gripping detective story.

beats.speech: Gripping. It means so exciting that you cannot stop reading or watching. It was a gripping detective story.

card.headline: Intriguing
card.meaning: interesting because it is strange or mysterious
card.example: He received an intriguing letter with no name on it.

beats.speech: Intriguing. It means interesting because it is strange or mysterious. He received an intriguing letter with no name on it.

card.headline: Absorbing
card.meaning: so interesting that you forget everything else
card.example: The puzzle was so absorbing that I lost track of time.

beats.speech: Absorbing. It means so interesting that you forget everything else. The puzzle was so absorbing that I lost track of time.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:

She gave a captivating speech.
It was a gripping detective story.
He received an intriguing letter with no name on it.
The puzzle was so absorbing that I lost track of time.
